newsitem.title: USA: UN's Eitel sees mid-Dec oil-for-food deal start.
newsitem.headline: UN's Eitel sees mid-Dec oil-for-food deal start.

text.p: The head of the UN's sanctions committee on Iraq said he expects the UN-Iraq oil-for-food deal to start in mid-December.
German Ambassador Tono Eitel, head of the sanctions panel, said Tuesday "there is a fair chance" for final UN implementation of the deal in the coming days.
"It is my personal feeling, unofficially...that by mid-December there is a fair chance to get the report," Eitel said, referring to the final UN okay.

Under terms of the oil-for-food accord, UN Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali must report to the security council that all issues pertaining to implementing the deal are complete, thus allowing Iraqi oil sales to begin.

Eitel said sanctions committee members were informed that Dutch firm Saybolt personnel were to inspect a key oil metering station in the next two days. Eitel noted that "nobody expected greater delays (caused) by the inspection of the metering stations."

Saybolt inspectors were specifically to ensure metering equipment was functioning properly at the Zakho oil terminal along the Iraqi-Turkish border. Inspectors previously found faulty metering equipment at the Zakho station.

Under the oil-for-aid scheme, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months in order to buy food and supplies for civilians suffering from sanctions imposed by the UN after Baghdad invaded Kuwait in 1990.
